newsitem.title: INDIA: India coalition leftists oppose oil price rise - PTI.
newsitem.headline: India coalition leftists oppose oil price rise - PTI.

text.p: The Communist Party of India said on Saturday it will oppose any increase in subsidised petroleum product prices when the United Front coalition's steering committee meets on July 8 to discuss the subject.

Press Trust of India reported CPI's general secretary A.B. Bardhan as saying at a news conference in the western city of Ahmedabad that his party was "totally against any move by the United Front government to raise the price of petroleum products."
Bardhan said he would would stick to this viewpoint when he met other members of the steering committee on Tuesday.
The steering committee has failed at two earlier meetings to agree a way of repaying oil companies money due to them for selling products below market prices.

At the end of the last fiscal year on March 31 the companies were owed 155 billion rupees ($4.32 billion) from the oil pool account, and the bill was rising, albeit more slowly as world prices have fallen.
Indian refiners have had to borrow heavily to pay for crude feedstocks, while the sole importer of crude oil into the country, Indian Oil Corp, has had to borrow most of all.
The oil payments crisis has led to investment deferrals which has hurt domestic oil output.
Bardhan said the government should frame a mix of short- and long-term measures to tackle to oil pool deficit.
He called for more investments in exploration and production to check the rising import bill.
The government should also cap the manufacturing of private vehicles and limit import of cars enginges over 1000 cc, he said.
